verdict.rationale: Lium is a GPU rental marketplace for NVIDIA GPUs. Its CLI documents renting an H100 directly, and rent-by-spec picks the cheapest node matching a GPU spec, which points to a choice of GPU types. However, nothing in the evidence names H200 or B200 availability or any specific cheaper previous-generation GPUs. Missing for 10: documented H200/B200 availability, named previous-generation options (e.g. A100/older), a published GPU catalog or price list showing the range, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an ML engineer, I can choose from current-generation datacenter GPUs (H100/H200/B200 class) as well as cheaper previous-generation options

citations.quote: rents the cheapest node matching a GPU spec under a `max_price_per_gpu_hour` ceiling
Lium (lium.io) is a GPU rental marketplace: rent NVIDIA GPUs by the hour, billed per second.
